content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to a single disputed point and rests that verdict on what one verse-pair (Luke 2:48-49) says, which is the kind of single-verse ground the rule addresses.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "Whether reasoning that one verse's phrase is 'qualified' by the next verse is a ground about the content of a single verse, or a ground that the single verse fails to state a link or its contrary; I read the qualification as a single-verse failure to establish the father-link, so it falls under the rule.", "why": "The judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED on the single Luke 2:48-49 exchange as failing to establish the father-link, which the rule forbids as a ground, and the definition's note that single-verse status is never the deciding test is not applied."}
